subject: Immediate exec attention: Persephone Labs throughput clamp & token window misalignment
messages:
From: Sasha Ivanov <sasha@persephonelabs.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: support@persephonelabs.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Persephone Labs observing sustained 429s and throughput clamp

Marissa / Redwood team —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 429s and end-to-end latency across our production traffic starting ~08:50 PT. Error rate climbed to ~12% for our worst endpoints, and throughput dropped by ~40% despite normal user demand. Attached is a snapshot of our dashboard (timeseries + distribution) — you can see the sudden step down in accepted requests.

We suspect a rate/quotas change on your side because we didn't change our traffic profile. Can you confirm any policies or maintenance that could cause a global clamp, and advise next steps? This is impacting a scheduled demo for a prospective customer in 2 hours.

Sasha Ivanov
Head of Platform Reliability
Persephone Labs

From: dev.patel@redwood.com <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Persephone Labs observing sustained 429s and throughput clamp

Marissa / Grace —

I've pulled the live policy matrices and throttle logs for Persephone's project. Quick summary of findings:

- At 08:48 PT we observed a simultaneous enforcement of a project-level QPS floor (safety guardrail) and a per-customer burst credit reclamation job. The reclamation job was scheduled to run every 60s but a recent change doubled the reclamation aggressiveness.
- The combination caused the request admission controller to drop requests once per short window, appearing as a sustained clamp because the reclamation removed credits faster than the runtime could replenish KV cache hits.
- Additionally, there is an overlap between the token-window boundary for streaming requests and the per-route microburst allowance — when long streaming sessions produce many small requests, they hit the per-route microburst and exhaust burst credits prematurely.

Proposed immediate mitigation (15–30m):
1) Temporarily increase the project-level burst_window_ms from 1000 -> 3000 for Persephone's project id to smooth credit replenishment (quick config patch attached).
2) Reduce reclamation aggressiveness flag (reclaim_rate = 0.5) for the next 2 hours and monitor.
3) Add temporary exception to per-route microburst enforcement for their top-3 production routes (we can scope by route id).

I'll push a canary patch to staging and roll to their project after Canary passes. Risks: creates small exposure to transient spikes for 10–15 minutes while we observe; CPU utilization may increase slightly.

Attachments: quick_config_patch.yaml

Dev Patel
On-call, Inference Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

Subject: Persephone incident post-mitigation + exec ask (credits & config change)

Lauren / Karthik — quick recap and ask:

Summary:
- Root cause: overlapping enforcement between project-level safety guardrail and a newly aggressive burst-credit reclamation job; long streaming sessions triggered per-route microburst exhaustion.
- Impact: intermittent 429s and latency for Persephone from ~08:48–09:20 PT, peak error rate ~12%, throughput down ~40% on a set of routes.
- Immediate action taken: Dev applied the temporary patch (increased burst_window_ms, lowered reclaim_rate, exempted top-3 routes). Canary completed at 10:58 PT; mitigation rolled at 11:05 PT. Metrics returned to baseline within ~10 minutes.

Next steps (owners & timeline):
- Infra (Dev): implement a permanent nuance in the reclamation job to account for streaming sessions and extend burst-window logic. ETA: 2 sprints (by 2026-07-05).
- Product / Policy (Karthik): review default reclaim aggressiveness and publish a clearer doc describing microburst vs. project-level settings. ETA: 1 sprint.
- CS (Grace): customer-facing postmortem and goodwill credit proposal for the impacted demo.

Ask: please approve a one-time credit of $3,500 to Persephone Labs for the interruption while we complete the permanent fix. This is on the conservative side given demo impact and our SLA language.

I've attached the quick runbook and the config patch applied. I'm happy to join a short call if you want more detail.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
